developments: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive and left its board with immediate effect; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and Nvidia shares fell about 10% before the US open.
Bitcoin broke below $72,000 and touched about $71,100, its weakest level since August, as over $650 million of mostly long positions were liquidated across crypto.
Futures now price about a 94% chance of a December Fed rate rise, with the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%.
briefing.changed: This morning bitcoin was holding $73,500 and the Nvidia story was unresolved. Since then Huang has gone, bitcoin has lost another $2,000, leveraged longs have been flushed out, and Zcash slipped further below $1,000. The Nasdaq itself held up better than Nvidia, so the shock has hit crypto harder than stocks.
briefing.question: Is the drop to $71,000 a leverage flush that runs its course, or the start of a test of $70,000 while ETF money keeps leaving?
briefing.watch: The US close at 21:00 UK, then US PPI on Friday 13 November at 13:30 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Huang quits Nvidia as bitcoin slides to lowest since August
lead.standfirst: Nvidia's founder resigned with immediate effect on Thursday, and bitcoin fell through $72,000 as more than $650 million of crypto bets were liquidated.
body: Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive and director of Nvidia with immediate effect, the company's board announced at 13:48 UK time on Thursday. Chief financial officer Colette Kress became interim chief executive and Harvey Jones was named the board's first chair, StockTitan reported, citing Nvidia's filing with the SEC.

Nvidia shares were down about 10% before the US open, wiping roughly $440 billion off its market value, but the Nasdaq was down only about 0.35% by mid-morning in New York, according to CoinDesk. Nvidia still plans to report results on 17 November.

Bitcoin fared worse. It fell below $72,000 and touched about $71,100 on Kraken, its weakest level since August. Coinglass data cited by Bitcoin.com showed more than $656 million of crypto positions liquidated in 24 hours, about $555 million of them longs.
Fund flows added to the pressure. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.44 billion over five sessions to 11 November, according to SoSoValue data reported by Decrypt.
Rates kept rising. Markets priced about a 94% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate rise on 9 December, and the 10-year Treasury yield stood above 5%, CoinDesk reported.
Zcash fell to about $955. Traders now turn to the US close and Friday's producer price figures at 13:30 UK.

headline: Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia and bitcoin fell below $72,000 to its lowest since August as over $650 million of leveraged bets were wiped out. Fed hike odds rose to about 94% and ETF outflows hit $1.44 billion in five days.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, afternoon edition. The mood is risk-off. Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's chief executive with immediate effect, and its shares fell about ten per cent, though the wider Nasdaq held up. Bitcoin fell below seventy-two thousand dollars, touching about seventy-one thousand one hundred, its lowest since August, as more than six hundred and fifty million dollars of crypto bets were liquidated. Bitcoin funds have lost one point four billion dollars in five days. Markets now see a ninety-four per cent chance of a Fed rate rise in December. Zcash is about nine hundred and fifty-five dollars. Next, watch US producer prices on Friday at half past one. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Colette Kress named interim chief
stories.why: This morning the board's decision was unknown. At 08:48 ET (13:48 UK) Nvidia said Huang had resigned as CEO and director with immediate effect; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Harvey Jones is chair. Shares were down about 10% premarket at $155.44, but by 10:00 ET Nvidia was down about 7% and the Nasdaq only about 0.35%, CoinDesk reported. Results are still due on 17 November.

note.read: Removing the uncertainty quickly kept the damage mostly inside Nvidia; the wider tech market did not crack, so this alone does not explain bitcoin's fall.
note.alt: A leaderless Nvidia could weigh on the whole AI trade over the coming weeks, especially if the 17 November results or guidance disappoint.
note.change: A broad Nasdaq sell-off into the close, or weak Nvidia guidance on 17 November, would make this a wider risk-off driver.

stories.title: Bitcoin breaks below $72,000 to its lowest since August as $656m is liquidated
stories.why: Bitcoin was about $71,630 on Kraken at 16:30 UK, after a low of $71,133, down from about $73,500 this morning. Coinglass data cited by Bitcoin.com showed $656 million of crypto liquidations in 24 hours, about $555 million longs and $237 million in BTC, with the sharpest burst around 13:15 UK. CoinDesk called it the weakest level since mid-to-late August.
stories.caveat: Analysts point to $70,000 as the next level to watch; that is opinion, not fact.

note.read: This morning's warning signs (holders selling at a loss, shrinking stablecoin supply) played out: with little fresh buying, a crowded long position was flushed.
note.alt: Large long liquidations often mark short-term exhaustion, and the Nasdaq's resilience suggests this was a crypto-specific leverage clear-out rather than a wider panic.
note.change: A recovery back above $73,000 would suggest the flush is done; a daily close below $70,000 would point to a deeper reset.

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs lose $1.44bn in five days; Wednesday's $300m outflow confirmed
stories.why: SoSoValue data reported by Decrypt confirms this morning's figure: $299.9 million out on Wednesday, $1.44 billion over 5 to 11 November and $1.88 billion so far in November. CoinDesk put about $270 million of Wednesday's outflow in BlackRock's IBIT, and Cointelegraph counted about $2 billion out of IBIT over nine sessions. Cumulative net inflows remain about $55 billion.

stories.title: December Fed hike odds rise to about 94% as the 10-year yield tops 5%
stories.why: Up from about 89% after Tuesday's CPI. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said policy needs to be restrictive and she prefers smaller, steady rises. US jobless claims rose to 200,000 (forecast 195,000) and existing home sales fell to 3.75 million, the lowest since 2010, CoinDesk reported. The dollar index is above 103 and gold fell to about $3,868.

stories.title: Zcash slips to about $955 as the only ZEC ETF loses $15m
stories.why: ZEC was about $955 on Kraken at 16:30 UK, after a low of $940.73, down from about $983 this morning, so the break below $1,000 is holding. CoinDesk reported the lone US ZEC ETF lost nearly $15 million in one session. The grants treasury vote from Monday is unchanged.

stories.title: Gemini sells its UK and European arm to stablecoin firm KAST for under $10m
stories.why: CoinDesk reported that Gemini is selling the UK and EU businesses it planned to wind down to Singapore-based KAST, citing one person familiar with the deal. Buyers have valued such units for their regulatory permissions, a sign of how scarce UK crypto licences are before the FCA regime. Neither firm commented; nothing was said about UK customers.

explained.title: What a liquidation cascade is
body: Traders who borrow to bet on a rise (longs) must keep enough collateral on the exchange. When the price falls far enough, the exchange closes the position automatically by selling. That forced selling pushes the price lower, which triggers the next layer of liquidations.

Cascades are fast and can overshoot. Once the crowded leverage is gone, the forced selling stops, which is why analysts watch liquidation totals for signs that a drop is exhausting itself, though that is never guaranteed.

Did ETF outflows continue on Thursday? Evidence: SoSoValue and Farside figures, published tonight UK time.
